Question ID: ALG1_U06_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.DF.6

A model predicts 50 students will attend. The actual attendance is 54. What is the residual?

feedback.text: This subtracts actual from predicted. This course uses actual minus predicted.
Residual = actual - predicted = 54 - 50 = 4.
This adds the two values instead of finding prediction error.
This is the predicted value, not the residual.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U06_L07_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.DF.8

Which survey method is most likely to produce a representative sample of a high school?

answer.text: Survey only students in the chess club

feedback.text: This sample may overrepresent one group of students.

answer.text: Survey only students arriving before 7:00 a.m.

feedback.text: This may miss students with different schedules.
This does not represent all grade levels.

answer.text: Randomly survey students from every grade level

feedback.text: Random selection across grade levels is more likely to represent the school.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U06_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.DF.9

In a two-way table, 16 students chose art and 24 students chose music. What is the row total for those choices?

feedback.text: Add the counts in the row: 16 + 24 = 40.
This includes only the music count, not the row total.
This subtracts the counts instead of adding them.
This multiplies the counts instead of totaling them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U06_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.DF.6

A residual is -6. What does this mean?

feedback.text: A residual of 0 would mean an exact prediction.

answer.text: The actual value was 6 more than predicted

feedback.text: That would produce a positive residual of 6.
A negative residual means actual was less than predicted.
A residual can be interpreted as prediction error.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG1_U06_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A1.DF.8

Why might a simulation be useful?

answer.text: It proves the exact outcome of one event

feedback.text: Simulations estimate patterns; they do not prove a single outcome.

answer.text: It estimates a chance process by repeating trials

feedback.text: Repeated trials can estimate likely outcomes.

answer.text: It removes the need to define an event

feedback.text: The event must be defined before a simulation can be useful.

answer.text: It guarantees the population is unbiased

feedback.text: Simulation and sampling bias are different issues.
